content.user_title: Map conversion values to profit-based bidding
content.value_statement: Revenue-only conversion values can make value-based bidding optimize for low-margin orders. This skill creates a documented conversion-value model and QA checklist using margin, COGS, and defensible proxy values.
actual_capabilities: Inventories revenue and non-revenue conversion actions.
Defines dynamic or static conversion value bases.
Applies margin or COGS adjustments to revenue values.
Derives proxy values for leads, calls, and signups from supplied inputs.
Checks platform conversion value against booked contribution.
Produces a launch-readiness decision and value QA sheet.
limitations: It does not verify event tags, UTMs, or conversion firing.
It does not reconcile duplicate credit across advertising platforms.
It requires user-provided revenue, margin, COGS, or close-rate data.
It does not connect to advertising platforms or change campaign settings.

use_cases.title: Prepare ecommerce tROAS values
use_cases.description: Map SKU or category margins onto dynamic purchase values before a tROAS launch.

use_cases.title: Value lead-generation actions
use_cases.description: Calculate documented proxy values for leads, phone calls, and signups from close-rate and order-value inputs.

use_cases.title: Review a bidding value model
use_cases.description: Compare recent platform conversion value with booked contribution and identify missing value inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Start with purchase values
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set conversion values for tROAS. I have purchase revenue and a blended margin of 42%.

prompt_templates.title: Create lead proxy values
prompt_templates.prompt: Create proxy values for leads and phone calls. Our average net order value is $180 and 18% of leads become customers.

prompt_templates.title: Choose value-rule design
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend static or dynamic conversion values. Our product categories have different margins, and I can provide category revenue and COGS exports.

prompt_templates.title: Run a value-model QA
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this conversion value model before launch. Compare the platform value total with our booked contribution and list any blockers.

output_examples.input: Purchase revenue is $200 and category margin is 35%.
Average net order value is $150 and lead-to-sale rate is 20%.
output: Status: Estimated until close rate is validated

output_examples.input: Platform conversion value is three times booked contribution.
output: Next step: review margin adjustment and conversion scope

best_practices: Use measured SKU or category margins when they are available.
Label each value as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
Reconcile recent platform value with booked contribution before launch.
anti_patterns: Do not use gross revenue when margin data materially changes profitability.
Do not assign round proxy values without a documented derivation.
Do not add value rules that double-adjust an already netted value.

faq.question: What is a conversion value model?
faq.answer: It defines the value sent to an advertising platform for each conversion action.

faq.question: Does this skill configure Google Ads or Meta?
faq.answer: No. It produces a value model and QA guidance from the data you provide.

faq.question: Can it use revenue without margin data?
faq.answer: Yes, but it marks the model as incomplete when profit-based bidding needs margin data.

faq.question: How are lead values calculated?
faq.answer: It multiplies expected net order value by the supplied lead-to-sale close rate.

faq.question: Does it check conversion tags?
faq.answer: No. Use a conversion signal QA process to verify event firing and UTM quality.

faq.question: Does it prevent cross-platform double counting?
faq.answer: No. Cross-platform attribution and order-ID reconciliation require a separate review.
